title: Data residency playbook: subprocessors, retention windows, and EU/UK transfer language
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a product + legal playbook that standardizes how we answer enterprise security questionnaires and negotiate data residency terms. Deliverables: (1) Subprocessor disclosure and approval flow for Hosted/Dedicated/Private customers, (2) Retention policy options and contract language for logs/inputs/outputs/KV caches, (3) Standardized EU/UK transfer text (SCCs + UK Addendum approach) and an exception matrix for customers needing on-prem or VPC installs, (4) Pricing/packaging experiments for residency as an add-on versus included in Dedicated contracts.
background: Increasingly large prospects and enterprise customers are requesting explicit contract language around where customer data is stored, which subprocessors process it, and retention guarantees for model inputs, outputs, and derivative telemetry (traces, logs, embeddings). Legal has been fielding bespoke redlines which slows sales. We need a pragmatic product + legal template to reduce negotiation friction and test pricing for residency guarantees.
proposed_solution: Deliver a two-track playbook: a standard template for Hosted customers with clear transfer mechanisms (EU SCCs + documented UK addendum acceptance path), and an enterprise template for Dedicated/Private customers that includes per-tenant residency commitments, explicit subprocessor list with 30-day change notifications, and configurable retention windows (30/90/365/never). Add a residency add-on pricing experiment with three tiers: Standard (no residency guarantee), Region-Scoped (data stored in region, +10% unit price), and Isolated (Dedicated pool or Private deploy, custom pricing).
acceptance_criteria: Legal-approved Hosted residency clause + EU SCCs wording saved in contract template library
Subprocessor disclosure process documented (email + console change log + 30-day opt-out for enterprise customers)
Retention options documented and represented in template (30/90/365/never) with default = 90 days for hosted
Pricing experiment spec for region-scoped and isolated tiers with telemetry hooks to measure deal throughput and ACV impact
Engineering checklist for implementing tenant-scoped storage and deletion endpoints for Dedicated and Hosted plans
decisions: Default retention for Hosted API will be 90 days with a 30-day deletion SLA after contract or feature opt-out; Dedicated and Private can set custom retention in contract
We will use the EU Standard Contractual Clauses as our baseline transfer mechanism and offer a UK Addendum for UK transfers; for customers that reject SCCs, offer Dedicated or Private deployment only
Subprocessor list will be published in the Console (legal page) and emailed to enterprise contacts on change with a 30-day notice window
Residency pricing will be run as an experiment with two paid tiers (Region-Scoped and Isolated) rather than baked into all Dedicated contracts initially
open_questions: What is the default data controller/processor language Legal will insist on for Hosted vs Dedicated? (Legal to confirm)
Is there a minimal SLO for deletion requests we can commit to across hosted customers beyond contractual deletion windows?
Do any of our cloud subprocessors require a separate disclosure cadence (e.g., third-party telemetry vendors)?
How will encryption key management options (customer-managed KMS vs Redwood-managed) affect residency guarantees and pricing?
